Chilliwack Mountain is a named mountain and hillside neighbourhood on the south side of the Fraser River, west of Chilliwack Creek and west of the downtown core.

The City publishes no street-by-street boundary for the Chilliwack Mountain sub-area; the residential streets climb from Chilliwack Mountain Road and Schweyey Road, with Grandview Drive rising to Hillkeep Place at the top.

Below the homes sits the Industrial Way / Progress Way industrial area on the valley floor; downtown and Chilliwack Proper West are east, Little Mountain is southeast, and Fairfield Island is across the river north.
The housing form here is single-detached houses on hillside lots, governed by the hillside permit areas in.

One townhouse complex is confirmed in City council records: Development Permit DP000817 for Cedarsky Developments Ltd. at 43660 and 43710 Chilliwack Mountain Road; the complex name is not stated in that record.
No condominium building on the mountain was confirmed on an official source.

blocks.text: Chilliwack Mountain: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Mountain-specific lot minimums differ by zone and slope: Hillside Residential (HR) requires 0.2 hectares (ha) with community water or 0.4 ha otherwise; Rural Hillside (RH) requires 8 ha; Suburban Hillside Residential (SHR) rises from 360 square metres (m²) in the lowest slope band to 990 m² in the highest; Suburban Residential (SR) starts at 650 m² fully serviced.
No neighbourhood plan for the mountain appears in Schedule B of the Chilliwack 2050 Official Community Plan (OCP); the mountain is covered by the hillside permit areas instead.

blocks.text: Chilliwack Mountain: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Hillkeep Regional Park, a 36-acre nature reserve at the top of the mountain on Hillkeep Place, has about 2 kilometres of hiking trails, a viewing platform, limited parking, and hours of 7 a.m. to sunset.
The nearest City leisure centre is off-mountain: Chilliwack Landing Leisure Centre, 9145 Corbould Street.
The nearest library branch is Chilliwack Library, 45860 First Avenue, downtown.
Chilliwack General Hospital, 45600 Menholm Road, is the hospital serving the mountain.

blocks.text: Chilliwack Mountain: development and new projects

items.t: Schweyey Road Forcemain Replacement, Schweyey Road below the mountain: the City replaced about 230 metres of 200-millimetre forcemain with a 500-millimetre high-density polyethylene forcemain serving Chilliwack Mountain and parts of Industrial Way and Progress Way. Status: completed June 2026, road paved (as of November 3, 2026).

The mountain angle is servicing cost risk, not a different tax rate: parcels outside the Schweyey Road forcemain catchment may face connection or on-site servicing costs that the City page does not price per lot.

No bus route climbs the mountain; the closest service is BC Transit Route 59 Industrial, which links Downtown Chilliwack and Cottonwood Mall via the Lickman Park & Ride in peak-period trips shown on the route schedule.
Highway 1 access is at the Lickman Road interchange south of the mountain, where the Lickman Park & Ride sits.

blocks.text: Chilliwack Mountain: risks and due diligence

items.t: Slope is the main check: Development Permit Area D-2 covers land identified with slope-instability and soil-erosion hazards, and Development Permit Area D-5 applies to slopes of 20 percent or more; look the lot up in the OCP Schedule D maps.
A qualified professional must submit a geotechnical study under the Engineers and Geoscientists British Columbia landslide-assessment guidelines before development proceeds in D-2.

At the mountain's base, the Chilliwack Creek corridor carries riparian and fish-habitat constraints; a federal assessment for a Schweyey Road stormwater outfall into Chilliwack Creek addressed designated critical habitat for Salish Sucker.
Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) status is parcel-specific; check any lot on Agricultural Land Commission mapping.

Chilliwack Mountain home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

18 townhomes sold in Chilliwack Mountain with a median price of $688,450 (the middle half sold between $660,625 and $731,250), taking a median of 26 days to sell at 97.9% of the last list price; 0% sold above list. They had a median $327 per square foot, a median year built of 2014 and a median strata fee of $395 a month. 9 houses sold in Chilliwack Mountain with a median price of $970,000 (the middle half sold between $850,000 and $1,095,000), taking a median of 15 days to sell at 97.1% of the last list price; 0% sold above list. They had a median $392 per square foot, a median year built of 1997 and a median lot of 10,450 square feet.

faq.a: Yes, in most cases. The whole mountain sits in Development Permit Area D-2, Hillside Environment, and a permit with a geotechnical hazard and slope assessment is required before subdivision, construction, land clearing or earthworks. Budget for the qualified professional's report and the permit timeline before committing to a build, an addition or major landscaping on any mountain lot.
faq.q: Do I need a special permit to build or clear land on Chilliwack Mountain?

faq.a: No to both. No British Columbia Transit (BC Transit) route in the Chilliwack list runs onto the mountain's residential streets, and no School District No. 33 (SD33) public school is located on the mountain in the provincial school directory. Families drive to valley-floor schools, and the catchment for any address is confirmed only in the SD33 School Locator.
faq.q: Is there a bus or a school on the mountain itself?

The City states the sanitary forcemain along Schweyey Road provides sewage services for Chilliwack Mountain and portions of Industrial Way and Progress Way. That statement does not confirm connection for a specific parcel, so verify water and sewer status for the exact lot with the City before writing an offer.

faq.a: Because slope sets the minimum in the SHR zone. The minimum lot area starts at 360 m² in the lowest slope band and rises to 990 m² in the highest band, so two lots of the same size can have different subdivision or rebuild potential. A lot's measured slope, not just its area, decides what the zoning allows.
